title: Comprehensive Ophthalmic Atlas: Keratitis, Dystrophies & Ectasias
summary: An exhaustive clinical reference guide for ophthalmology residents covering inflammatory corneal ulcers, dystrophies, and ectatic disorders. This poster synthesizes diagnostic criteria, management protocols, and investigative workups for complex anterior segment pathology.

sections.title: Peripheral Ulcerative Keratitis (PUK) Diagnostics
sections.content: Description: Slit lamp anterior segment coloured photo showing peripheral thinning and ulceration extending from 1 to 5 o'clock with limbal injection, with scleral thinning, I can see scleral hue otherwise rest of cornea clear. There is no kps. AC looks formed and hence no perforation, however I should assess the depth using focal slit beam. Patient is phakic, upper and lower lid show MGD. All of this picture consistent with peripheral ulcerative keratitis.

branches: Systemic: RA, SLE, Wegener’s, PAN, Relapsing Polychondritis, Sarcoidosis, Leukemia
Non-Infective: Mooren’s, Terrien’s, Marginal keratitis, Pellucid, Rosacea, Exposure, Neurotrophic, Trauma

sections.title: PUK Management Strategy
content: 1. Collaboration with rheumatologist for systemic immunosuppression
2. Systemic steroids (pulsed IV for acute phase)
3. Preservative-free topical lubricants
4. Prophylactic topical antibiotics (if epithelial defect)
5. Oral tetracycline (Doxycycline 100mg) for anti-collagenase effect
6. Avoid topical steroids (except possibly in Relapsing Polychondritis)
7. Surgical: Conjunctival excision or tectonic keratoplasty

rows: GAG deposits, stains with colloidal iron
Cone protrusion, Fleischer ring, Vogt striae

sections.title: Red Flags in PUK & Ectasia
content: Seidel sign positive: Indicates perforation
C-ANCA positive: Suggests Wegener’s granulomatosis (requires cyclophosphamide)
Graft rejection signs in post-PKP cases
Acute hydrops: Requires cycloplegics, aqueous suppressants, and NaCL 5% ointment

sections.title: Keratoconus Management (Dresden Protocol)
content: 1. Topical anaesthesia application.
2. Central 9 mm corneal epithelium removal.
3. 0.1% riboflavin administration every 1–5 min for 30 min.
4. UVA light exposure (3 mW/cm2, 365 nm) for 30 min (Total energy: 5.4 J/cm2).

content.explanation: Diagnostic indices for Keratoconus: Central K > 47.2D, I-S value > 1.2, Sim-K > 1.5D, SRAX > 21°.

sections.title: Pentacam Interpretation (Advanced Keratoconus)
content: K-Max front > 47.2D (Severe: >58D)
Thinnest location < 470 microns (Severe: <433 microns)
Elevation maps: Abnormal tongue shape, >15-20 micron deviation
ART-Max: Significantly low (<400 microns)
CTSP: Red line shows steep downward slope before 6mm zone
